text: The council approved the motion to award contracts for the purchase and delivery of new tires with an annual aggregate amount not to exceed $770,000 citywide.
The council will discuss a procurement study and allocate $250,000 for it later in the day.
The council will consider increasing local business preference in future RFPs, with a proposed increase from 5% to 15%.
There is a risk that local businesses may not receive a significant portion of the contract, despite the intent to support them.
The current local business preference may not be sufficient to meaningfully impact the local economy.

The City Council approved the ordinance establishing a 12-month moratorium on the issuance of building permits for new residential standalone construction along commercial and transportation corridors in West Long Beach.
The ordinance was declared urgent and will take effect immediately.
The matter will be referred to the Planning Commission and planning staff to initiate a study of potential amendments to existing zoning and building regulations.
Planning Commission and planning staff will conduct a study to align zoning and building regulations with the city's more recent land use and urban design elements of the general plan.
The moratorium could impact development timelines and potentially affect housing supply in the targeted areas.
There is a risk that the study may take longer than expected, delaying any potential updates to zoning and building regulations.
What specific changes to zoning and building regulations are expected to result from the study?

The council supports the execution of a Second Amendment to the Exclusive Negotiation Agreement with Howard CDB for the continuation of negotiations on the proposed development of the former Long Beach Armory.
Continue working with developers to finalize the project agreement and secure necessary grants.
Support the adaptive reuse of the Armory Building and the inclusion of 100% affordable housing.
The project may face delays due to the need for additional time to secure state and infrastructure grants.
There could be challenges in maintaining the momentum of negotiations with developers.
